newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela business views legal reform as urgent.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela business views legal reform as urgent.

text.p: Venezuela's private sector lacks confidence in the country's legal system and sees judicial insecurity as the single most important barrier to increased investment, Venezuela's National Investment Promotion Council (CONAPRI) said.
In a poll of 65 companies conducted over the second half of October, 84 percent believed judicial reform to be urgent.

"Although 54 percent of those polled felt positive or very positively about the success so far of Agenda Venezuela, the perception also existed that that success could be compromised by judicial insecurity," CONAPRI said in a press release.
Polled businesses saw judicial corruption, lack of transparency and predictability in judges' decisions, and inefficiency as the most pressing problems.

A $30 million World Bank judicial reform project that seeks to provide Venezuela's courts with technical and administrative aid recently collapsed after Venezuela's implementing agency, the Council of the Judiciary, abandoned it.
Gisela Parra, the council member that had hitherto led the project, was dismissed under a majority decision by the Council.
